ordered_step_reconstruction: For zeta=q partial_q z, its zero signed symplectic pairing with the scaling field makes the two component Wronskians equal on each cell. At event i, exact saltation gives w_i-w_(i-1)=alpha_i d_i with d_i=u_i/U_i-v_i/V_i and alpha_i=-2 Delta rho_i U_i^4/S_t(t_i)=-sigma a_i, a_i>0.

Exact two-frequency propagation between consecutive events gives d_(i+1)-d_i=K_i w_i, with K_i=[sin(theta_i)+mu sin(mu theta_i)]/[sqrt(rho_i)U_iU_(i+1)]. The accepted phase bound and transversality make every K_i finite and nonzero.

Eliminating d_i yields the symmetric path matrix with diagonal 1/a_i+1/a_(i+1)-sigma K_i and off-diagonal -1/a_(i+1). The scaling field maps to d=w=0, so the matrix acts on relative modes modulo the permanent scaling line.

For the log(q) field, w_0=0, d_1=-1 and w_1=sigma a_1. The final row of the path recurrence is L_sigma W=(w_m/a_m)e_last. Its corner cofactor is 1/[a_2...a_(m-1)det L_sigma], giving w_m=sigma(product_i a_i)det L_sigma. Direct m=2 calculation and continuant polynomial continuation verify the sign and the singular case.

At the common terminal, w_m=-q p partial_q U(L). Combining the accepted causal identity p partial_q U(L)=sigma(R-1)J gives w_m=-q sigma(R-1)J. The accepted symplectic endpoint identity gives partial_q A_n=(q^2-1)w_m/(q p^2r^2).

All remaining factors q, R-1, a_i, p^2 and r^2 are strictly positive in scope, so J<0 iff det(L_sigma)>0 iff sign(w_m)=sigma iff sign(partial_q A_n)=sigma. Vanishing of the determinant is equivalent only to simultaneous terminal position vanishing of the distinguished q-Jacobi line, not to the existence of an arbitrary Dirichlet Jacobi field.

The result stops at the exact equivalence. The universal determinant orientation is recorded as open, while L_sigma positive definite and full complementary inertia are correctly identified as stronger sufficient statements.
